# TimeAxisPath { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath }

```python
loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath()
```

Abstract definition of a time axis path through 2D space.

A TimeAxisPath maps 1D timeline coordinates to 2D image coordinates.
The path has a defined length (in timeline units, typically pixels)
and provides bidirectional coordinate conversion.

Subclasses implement specific geometric shapes:
- HorizontalLinePath: x = time, y = constant
- DiagonalLinePath: arbitrary straight line
- ParametricPath: x(t), y(t) functions for curves/spirals
- PiecewisePath: consecutive pieces, such as the accolades of a page

## Attributes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [length](#timetoalign.loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath.length) | Total length of this path in timeline units. |

### distance_to_path { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath.distance_to_path }

```python
loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath.distance_to_path(x, y)
```

Compute perpendicular distance from point to path.

Default implementation samples the path and finds minimum distance.
Subclasses may override with analytical solutions.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name   | Type                                                  | Description            | Default    |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|------------|
| x      | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | X coordinate in image. | _required_ |
| y      | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | Y coordinate in image. | _required_ |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                  | Description         |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
|        | [Number](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.Number`) | Distance in pixels. |

### from_boxes { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath.from_boxes }

```python
loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath.from_boxes(boxes, *, accolades=None)
```

Make the time path of one page from the areas drawn on it.

Each accolade becomes one :class:`HorizontalLinePath` spanning its
boxes exactly: ``x0`` is their least and ``x1`` their greatest x,
``y`` the middle of their y extent and ``tolerance`` half of that
extent, so the line's strip is the accolade's y extent. The middle
and the half are exact: an ``int`` where whole, else a ``Fraction``.

#### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type                                                                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                | Default    |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| boxes     | [Iterable](`collections.abc.Iterable`)\[[Shape](`timetoalign.core.Shape`) \| [Box](`timetoalign.core.Box`)\] | The areas of ONE page in reading order: shapes, or Box events (read through their shape), all of one unit and number type.                                                                                 | _required_ |
| accolades | [Sequence](`collections.abc.Sequence`)\[[int](`int`)\] \| None                                               | Per box, a label of its accolade (one label per box); the accolades follow each other in the order of their first box. When omitted, :func:`group_into_accolades` assigns them from the boxes' left edges. | `None`     |

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                | Description                                                  |
|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [PiecewisePath](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.PiecewisePath`) | The path, one piece per accolade (a ``PiecewisePath`` of one |
|        | [PiecewisePath](`timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.PiecewisePath`) | piece too).                                                  |

#### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | If no box is given, the boxes lie on two units or number types, *accolades* does not hold one label per box, or an accolade has no x extent (the message names it by its position, counted from 1). |

#### Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

Three measures, the third on a second line:

```python
>>> from timetoalign.core import BoundingBox
>>> measures = [
...     BoundingBox.from_corners(100, 50, 300, 90, unit="pixels"),
...     BoundingBox.from_corners(300, 52, 520, 95, unit="pixels"),
...     BoundingBox.from_corners(90, 150, 400, 190, unit="pixels"),
... ]
>>> path = TimeAxisPath.from_boxes(measures)
>>> path.pieces[0]
HorizontalLinePath(x0=100, x1=520, y=Fraction(145, 2), tolerance=Fraction(45, 2))
>>> path.pieces[1]
HorizontalLinePath(x0=90, x1=400, y=170, tolerance=20)
>>> path.offsets, path.length
((0, 420), 730)
>>> path.piece_of(measures[2])
1
```

### is_point_on_path { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.TimeAxisPath.is_point_on_path }
